Nasdaq slips as chip stocks retreat from highs

Published 2026-10-06 15:15 UTC

The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.8% on Thursday as semiconductor stocks retreated from record highs after a major brokerage downgraded several chipmakers. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 2%, its biggest one-day drop in a month, while the S&P 500 lost 0.3%.

The brokerage cut its rating on three chip companies to neutral, arguing that their share prices already reflect years of strong growth in artificial intelligence hardware. Its analysts wrote that customers have been building up inventory and that orders could slow next year as large technology firms digest the equipment they have already bought.

Shares of memory chip makers fell the most, with some losing more than 4%. Equipment suppliers that sell machines used to manufacture chips also declined. The selloff spread to other technology stocks that have benefited from enthusiasm about AI, including software companies and server makers.

Some investors saw the decline as a healthy pause after a strong run. The semiconductor index is still up more than 30% this year, and many fund managers remain overweight in the sector. Others said the downgrade highlights how much optimism is priced into the stocks and how sensitive they have become to any hint of slower demand.

Outside technology, defensive sectors such as consumer staples and health care gained as investors rotated into steadier businesses. Treasury yields were little changed, and the dollar edged higher against major currencies.

Traders are now looking ahead to next week's earnings reports from several large chip companies, which will offer a clearer view of orders and pricing. Analysts said comments about customer inventory levels and spending plans for 2027 will matter more than the quarterly results themselves.

Market strategists noted that semiconductor stocks now make up a larger share of the S&P 500 than at any point in two decades, so swings in the group have an outsized effect on broad indexes. Some advised clients to trim positions after the long rally.
